pattaya.title: Choose a place where investing and living become the same decision
pattaya.lead: Pattaya is no longer only a resort on the Gulf of Thailand. It has become one of the country's fastest-growing cities — a coastal economy with international demand, real infrastructure behind it, and a quality of life that keeps owners coming back.
pattaya.body1: The city sits inside the Eastern Economic Corridor, Thailand's flagship development zone, and roughly two hours from Bangkok's international airport. Motorway, rail and marina projects continue to reshape the coastline, and each one shortens the distance between Pattaya and the rest of Asia.
pattaya.body2: For an owner, that combination is unusual: a holiday destination with year-round arrivals, a resident international community, and a property market where a finished sea-view apartment still costs a fraction of its European equivalent.
pattaya.imageAlt: Aerial view of Pattaya bay and its coastal skyline at dusk

stats.label: Rental season that never really closes

points.title: The tropics, on your doorstep
points.body: Jomtien and Pratumnak beaches, the islands off Koh Larn, national parks inland, and a climate that makes the balcony the most-used room in the apartment.

points.title: Visitors from everywhere
points.body: Millions of international travellers pass through the region each year, from Europe, the Gulf and across Asia. That flow is what underwrites short-let occupancy.

points.title: A life, not just a line item
points.body: Marinas, golf, international schools, private hospitals and a restaurant scene that spans street food to fine dining. People invest here and then find reasons to stay.

ownership.title: How a foreign buyer owns property in Thailand
ownership.lead: Buying inside a condominium is the most straightforward route into the Thai market, and the one with the clearest legal footing for a foreign owner. Four steps, and none of them require you to be in the country.
ownership.imageAlt: Architectural drawings, a brass key and a document folder on a dark desk

steps.title: Buy inside the foreign quota
steps.body: Thai law allows up to 49% of a condominium building's saleable floor area to be registered to foreign owners. Units within that quota are available to you personally, as freehold.

steps.title: Send the funds from abroad
steps.body: The purchase money must arrive in Thailand from an overseas account in foreign currency. The receiving bank then issues the certificate that documents it — the paperwork the land office will ask for.

steps.title: Register at the land office
steps.body: Ownership is recorded in your name at the provincial Land Department and the title is issued to you. With a power of attorney, we complete this on your behalf.

steps.title: Hold it outright
steps.body: Freehold condominium title is yours indefinitely. It can be rented out, sold on, or passed to your heirs — it is not a lease and it does not expire.

ownership.note: This is a plain-language summary, not legal advice. Every purchase we handle is reviewed by an independent Thai lawyer before anything is signed, and we introduce you to one at the start rather than the end.

aurea-bayfront.name: Aurea Bayfront Residences
aurea-bayfront.tagline: Beachfront living on the Jomtien seafront
aurea-bayfront.summary: A 44-storey tower set directly on the Jomtien beachfront, with a sky pool on the fortieth floor and a residents' beach club at ground level. Every unit above the tenth floor holds an unobstructed sea view.
aurea-bayfront.body: Aurea is the developer's flagship on the southern coastline, and the last remaining beachfront plot of its size in the district. The building is arranged so that circulation sits inland and living space faces the water — a simple decision that gives almost every apartment a sea outlook rather than a side glance at one. Handover is fully furnished, and the developer's rental programme is available to owners from completion.
highlights: Sky pool and lounge on level 40

celeste-skyline.name: Celeste Skyline Residences
celeste-skyline.tagline: Panoramic bay views from Pratumnak Hill
celeste-skyline.summary: Thirty-eight floors on the quiet side of Pratumnak Hill, looking north across the whole sweep of Pattaya Bay. Larger layouts, lower density, and a private sky lounge on the top floor.
celeste-skyline.body: Pratumnak has long been the address for buyers who want the bay without the boulevard. Celeste takes that position and adds scale: generous one- to three-bedroom layouts, ceilings above the market standard, and a managed rental programme with a track record on the developer's two previous towers. The hill location means the view is protected by topography rather than by promises.
highlights: Private sky lounge and infinity edge pool

verdana-lagoon.name: Verdana Lagoon Suites
verdana-lagoon.tagline: A low-rise resort address in Na Jomtien
verdana-lagoon.summary: Completed and occupied. Eight low-rise buildings arranged around an 1,800 m² lagoon pool in Na Jomtien, a short drive south of the city and a minute from the water.
verdana-lagoon.body: Verdana is the option for a buyer who wants the asset earning now rather than in three years. The scheme is finished, the landscaping has matured, and occupancy is already established across the rental pool. Density is deliberately low — eight buildings of eight floors rather than a single tower — which is what keeps the resort feeling like a resort in high season.
highlights: Ready to move in and already renting
1,800 m² lagoon pool at the centre of the scheme

meridian-grand.name: Meridian Grand Tower
meridian-grand.tagline: Central Pattaya, a walk from Beach Road
meridian-grand.summary: Forty-one floors in the centre of the city, with a double-height sky lobby and both bay and city outlooks. The strongest short-let demand of anything in the portfolio.
meridian-grand.body: Location does the work here. Meridian sits within walking distance of Beach Road, Central Festival and the Walking Street end of the bay, which is precisely the catchment that drives nightly rates in high season. The developer has kept unit sizes efficient and the amenity deck generous — a combination built for rental performance rather than for the brochure.
highlights: City and bay outlooks from level 12 up
Highest short-let demand in our portfolio

seranai-wongamat.name: Seranai Wongamat Penthouses
seranai-wongamat.tagline: Ninety-six residences on the northern beach
seranai-wongamat.summary: A completed boutique tower on Wongamat Beach — the quiet northern stretch — with only ninety-six residences and duplex penthouses on the upper three floors.
seranai-wongamat.body: Wongamat is where long-term residents go when they have already tried the rest of the coast. Seranai is small by local standards and priced accordingly: fewer, larger apartments, a private beach frontage, and a service model closer to a hotel than a condominium. The upper duplexes are the largest freehold layouts we currently represent.
highlights: Only 96 residences with private beach frontage
Duplex penthouses on the upper three floors

palmera-bangsaray.name: Palmera Bangsaray Villas
palmera-bangsaray.tagline: Thirty-four private pool villas by the sea
palmera-bangsaray.summary: A gated enclave of thirty-four three- and four-bedroom villas in Bangsaray, each with a private pool, twenty minutes south of Pattaya and a few hundred metres from the beach.
palmera-bangsaray.body: Bangsaray is the fishing village that Pattaya's growth has not yet reached, and that is the entire appeal. Palmera is built for buyers who want land and space rather than a floor number: single-storey and duplex villas on private plots, with a residents' beach pavilion and a management company handling the villas as short-let stock when owners are away.

zenith-pattaya.name: ZENITH Pattaya
zenith-pattaya.tagline: A fully furnished 35 m² one-bedroom residence
zenith-pattaya.summary: A ready-to-move-in resale residence in ZENITH Pattaya, finished in a refined black, marble and cream palette with a smart one-bedroom layout.
zenith-pattaya.body: This 35 m² residence combines a polished interior, integrated kitchen, mirrored detailing and hotel-style bathrooms in one of Pattaya's established resort residences. The one-bedroom property is available for resale and can be viewed by appointment.
highlights: Premium marble finishes and fitted kitchen

zenith-pattaya-2.name: Zenith Pattaya 2
zenith-pattaya-2.tagline: A ready-to-move-in 65 m² resort condominium near Jomtien Beach
zenith-pattaya-2.summary: A modern eight-storey resort condominium in the Tappraya area, planned around lagoon pools, Japanese gardens and more than 900 residences.
zenith-pattaya-2.body: Zenith Pattaya 2 is a ready-to-move-in 65 m² residence with convenient access to Jomtien Beach, cafés, markets and the main roads. The property is available to view by appointment, with prices currently available on request.
highlights: Lagoon pools, Japanese gardens and resort amenities

about.title: Advice first. The transaction follows.
about.lead: I have spent years in the Pattaya market, and the part that matters is rarely the listing — it is knowing which developer delivers on time, which building will still rent in five years, and which deal is not worth doing.
about.body1: Grand Property was built around direct developer relationships and independent advice. You get access to the same inventory at the same price you would get walking into a sales gallery yourself, without the commission layer, and with someone on your side of the table reading the contract.
about.body2: Whether you are buying a sea-view apartment to rent out, moving capital out of Europe, or planning a life that starts somewhere warmer — the process should be clear, documented and calm. That is the whole job.
about.closing2: Let's build your position in Thailand.

page.title: A property practice, not a listings site
page.lead: Grand Property advises international buyers on acquiring, holding and eventually selling residential property in Thailand. We work with a small number of developers, a short list of projects, and clients who intend to keep the asset.
page.story1: Most people arrive in Pattaya's property market through a search engine and a sales gallery, in that order. They are shown whatever is paying the highest commission that month, told the yield figure that closes fastest, and left alone the day the transfer completes. It works — for everyone except the buyer.
page.story2: Grand Property was set up to invert that. We contract directly with developers, so our income does not depend on which building you choose. We put an independent Thai lawyer in front of you before you sign anything. And we stay involved after handover, because a rental apartment that nobody manages is not an investment, it is an expense.
page.mission: To make owning property in Thailand as considered, documented and unremarkable as owning property at home — for buyers who are doing it from four thousand miles away.
page.expertise1: We track completions, handover delays, resale prices and rental occupancy across the districts we sell in. That record is what lets us tell you which project is worth a four-year payment plan and which one is worth walking away from.
page.expertise2: It also means we can be specific. Not 'strong rental demand', but what a two-bedroom on that street actually achieved last high season, and what it sat empty for in May.

philosophy.title: We start with the brief, not the inventory
philosophy.body: Budget, timeframe, whether this is a yield play or a future home, and what you would need to see to walk away. The shortlist comes after that conversation.

philosophy.title: Everything in writing
philosophy.body: Reservation terms, payment schedule, what is included at handover, and what happens if the developer is late. In your language, before any money moves.

philosophy.title: Independent legal review
philosophy.body: A Thai lawyer who is not paid by the developer reads the contract and confirms the unit sits inside the foreign quota.

philosophy.title: We are still here in year three
philosophy.body: Rental placement, maintenance, tax filing support and resale. The relationship is meant to outlast the transaction.

page.consultantBody: Based in Pattaya and working with buyers across Europe and Asia. Fluent in the practical detail of Thai property — the quota, the transfer, the tax, the management contract — and blunt about the deals that do not stack up.

hero.title: A gateway to Asia
hero.lead: Strategically placed at the centre of Southeast Asia, with an open condominium market, a deep tourism economy and a currency cycle that runs independently of Europe. If you are looking for somewhere to invest, protect capital outside the eurozone, or make a genuine change of life, this is a region that offers all three at once.
hero.imageAlt: Aerial view of a tropical Thai coastline at golden hour

why.title: Strategic position
why.body: Bangkok is within a few hours' flight of every major market in the region — Singapore, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Ho Chi Minh City, and onward to China and India. Thailand is where Asia connects.

why.title: An economy built on arrivals
why.body: Tens of millions of international visitors a year sustain a hospitality and rental economy that very few property markets can match at this price level.

why.title: An open market for foreign buyers
why.body: The Condominium Act gives foreign nationals a clear, registered route to freehold apartment ownership. No company structure, no nominee, no workaround.

why.title: Capital outside Europe
why.body: A hard asset in a different currency, a different regulatory regime and a different economic cycle — the practical definition of diversification.

thailand.climate1: Thailand's Eastern Economic Corridor — the industrial and infrastructure programme covering Chonburi, Rayong and Chachoengsao — has channelled sustained public and private investment into exactly the stretch of coast where Pattaya sits. High-speed rail, airport expansion and motorway upgrades are the visible part of it.
thailand.climate2: For a property owner the effect is indirect but real: better connections mean more residents, more corporate tenants and more weekend arrivals from Bangkok. Infrastructure is slow, but it is the most reliable thing a coastal market can have behind it.
thailand.lifestyle1: The everyday case is simpler. Warm water eleven months of the year, islands within an hour of the shore, private healthcare at a fraction of European cost, international schools, golf, marinas, and food that ranges from a hundred-baht plate on the street to a tasting menu on the fortieth floor.
thailand.lifestyle2: Cost of living remains low relative to Western Europe, and the residency and long-stay visa options available to retirees, remote workers and investors have widened considerably in recent years.
thailand.ctaBody: Tell us the budget, the horizon and whether this is a yield decision or a life decision. We will come back with a shortlist and the numbers behind it.
